questions.question_text: Describe two differences between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell.

points: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus / their genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus (eukaryotic cells have a nucleus)
Prokaryotic DNA is a single loop (free in the cytoplasm)
Prokaryotic cells may contain plasmids (eukaryotic cells do not)
Prokaryotic cells are much smaller than eukaryotic cells
Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria or chloroplasts
Prokaryotic cell walls are not made of cellulose
scheme.guidance: Each mark needs a difference, i.e. a comparison or a feature clearly stated for one type of cell. 'Bacteria are prokaryotes' alone scores nothing.

questions.question_text:
A student looks at a cheek cell under a light microscope at ×400 magnification. The image of the cell is 6 mm long.

Calculate the real length of the cell in micrometres (µm). Show your working.

points: Uses real size = image size ÷ magnification
Converts to micrometres: 0.015 × 1000 = 15 µm
scheme.guidance: A correct final answer of 15 µm with no working scores all 3 marks. 0.015 mm (not converted) scores 2. Allow error carried forward from a wrong first step for the conversion mark.

questions.question_text: Explain why root hair cells must use active transport to absorb mineral ions from the soil.

points: The concentration of mineral ions in the soil is lower than in the root hair cell
So the ions must move against the concentration gradient (from dilute to concentrated)
This needs energy from respiration
Root hair cells have many mitochondria to release this energy
scheme.guidance: Do not credit 'by diffusion' or 'by osmosis'. 'Against the gradient' without saying which way the concentrations differ can still score the second mark.

questions.question_text:
Scientists are researching the use of embryonic stem cells to treat conditions such as diabetes and paralysis.

Evaluate the use of embryonic stem cells in medicine.

levels.descriptor: A detailed and balanced evaluation: clear advantages and disadvantages, accurate biology, and a reasoned conclusion or judgement.
Some advantages and disadvantages with some explanation, or a one-sided answer that is well explained. A conclusion may be missing or not supported.
Simple statements about stem cells or their uses, with little or no evaluation.

indicative: Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into any type of cell
They could replace damaged or missing cells, e.g. insulin-producing cells for diabetes or nerve cells for paralysis
Therapeutic cloning gives cells with the patient's own genes, so they are not rejected
Embryos are destroyed, which some people object to for ethical or religious reasons
Risk of transferring viral infection, and possible risk of cells dividing uncontrollably (cancer)
The treatments are still experimental and not guaranteed to work
Adult stem cells are an alternative but can only form a limited range of cells
A judgement weighing benefits against risks
scheme.guidance: Evaluate needs both sides and a judgement. An answer with no conclusion cannot reach the top of Level 3.

questions.question_text: Explain how the shape of an enzyme's active site is related to its function, and why enzymes stop working at high temperatures.

points: The active site has a specific shape
Only a substrate with a complementary shape fits the active site (lock and key)
At high temperatures the bonds holding the enzyme's shape break, so the active site changes shape (the enzyme is denatured)
The substrate no longer fits, so no enzyme-substrate complex forms and the reaction stops
scheme.guidance: 'The enzyme dies' or 'the enzyme is killed' scores nothing. 'Same shape as the substrate' is not credited; it must be complementary.

questions.question_text:
Coronary heart disease can be treated with stents or with statins.

Evaluate the use of stents and statins to treat coronary heart disease.

levels.descriptor: A balanced evaluation of both treatments with accurate biology, comparing them, and a supported judgement.
Some advantages or disadvantages of both treatments, or a good evaluation of only one. Judgement weak or missing.
Simple descriptions of what one or both treatments do, with little evaluation.

indicative: In coronary heart disease fatty material builds up in the coronary arteries, narrowing them and reducing blood flow to the heart muscle
Stents keep the artery open so blood can flow; they work immediately
Stents need surgery (with risks such as infection or bleeding) and the artery can narrow again; blood clots can form
Statins lower blood cholesterol, slowing the build-up of fatty material
Statins don't need surgery and can prevent future problems, but must be taken long-term and take time to work
Statins can have side effects, e.g. liver problems
Judgement, e.g. stents for severe blockages and statins for prevention, or both together
scheme.guidance: Both treatments must be evaluated to reach Level 3.

questions.question_text: Describe how white blood cells help to defend the body against pathogens.

points: Phagocytosis: white blood cells engulf and digest pathogens
They produce antibodies that target specific pathogens
They produce antitoxins that neutralise toxins made by bacteria
scheme.guidance: 'Fight' or 'kill germs' alone is not enough for a mark.

questions.question_text: Explain how vaccination stops a person becoming ill if they are later infected with the same pathogen.

points: The vaccine contains a small amount of dead or inactive pathogen
This stimulates white blood cells to produce specific antibodies
Memory cells remain in the body
If infected later, antibodies are produced rapidly and in large amounts
So the pathogen is destroyed before it can make the person ill
scheme.guidance: Max 4. Do not credit 'the vaccine contains antibodies'.

questions.question_text:
A farmer grows tomatoes in a greenhouse.

Explain how the farmer could increase the rate of photosynthesis of the tomato plants, and why increasing these conditions only increases the yield up to a point.

levels.descriptor: Several factors linked to how they increase photosynthesis, and a clear explanation of limiting factors and why yield stops increasing.
Some factors with some explanation, with a partial idea of limiting factors.
One or two factors named with little or no explanation.

indicative: Increase light intensity, e.g. with lamps
Increase carbon dioxide concentration, e.g. with paraffin heaters
Increase temperature, e.g. with heaters, because enzymes in photosynthesis work faster
The factor in shortest supply limits the rate (limiting factor)
Once one factor is increased, another becomes limiting, so the rate levels off
Too high a temperature denatures enzymes, so the rate falls
The extra cost of heating and lighting must be balanced against the extra profit
scheme.guidance: To reach Level 3 the answer must explain the limiting-factor idea, not just list conditions.

questions.subtopic: The nervous system and reflex actions
questions.question_text:
A person touches a hot pan and quickly pulls their hand away.

Describe the pathway of this reflex action.

points: Receptors in the skin detect the heat (stimulus)
An electrical impulse travels along a sensory neurone to the spinal cord / CNS
The impulse passes to a relay neurone
Then along a motor neurone to the effector
The effector is a muscle, which contracts to pull the hand away
Impulses cross synapses by chemicals diffusing between neurones
scheme.guidance: Max 4. The neurones must be in the right order to credit them. 'Signal goes to the brain' is not credited for a reflex.

questions.subtopic: Hormonal control and blood glucose regulation
questions.question_text:
After a meal, the concentration of glucose in a person's blood rises.

Explain how the body brings the blood glucose concentration back to normal.

points: The rise is detected by the pancreas
The pancreas releases insulin into the blood
Insulin causes glucose to move from the blood into cells
In the liver and muscles, excess glucose is converted to glycogen for storage
scheme.guidance: Do not credit 'insulin turns glucose into glycogen' unless the liver or muscles are mentioned. Glucagon is not relevant here.

questions.question_text:
Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele, f. Two parents are both carriers (Ff).

Use a Punnett square to determine the probability that their child will have cystic fibrosis. Describe your Punnett square in words if you can't draw it.

points: Gametes from each parent are F and f
Offspring genotypes FF, Ff, Ff, ff
Probability of cystic fibrosis (ff) is 0.25 / 25% / 1 in 4 / 1:3
scheme.guidance: A correct probability with no working scores 1 mark only. A ratio of 1:4 is wrong.

questions.subtopic: The theory of evolution and evidence
questions.question_text:
MRSA is a strain of bacteria that is resistant to many antibiotics.

Explain how a population of antibiotic-resistant bacteria develops.

points: A random mutation occurs in a bacterium's DNA
The mutation gives resistance to the antibiotic
The antibiotic kills the non-resistant bacteria
The resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
The allele / gene for resistance is passed on to the offspring
The population of resistant bacteria increases (natural selection)
scheme.guidance: Max 5. Do not credit 'bacteria become immune' or 'bacteria adapt to the antibiotic'.

questions.question_text: Describe the role of microorganisms in the carbon cycle.

points: Microorganisms decompose dead plants and animals, and waste
They respire, releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
This carbon dioxide is taken in by plants for photosynthesis
Decay returns mineral ions to the soil
